analysis:
Examined the docs/reference/configuration.md changes and the new RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift. The docs change (head lines 400-401) only adds two env-var rows, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. Both are documented as defaulting on and disableable only by 0/false/no/off. Both are marked 'Not forwarded to LaunchAgents', so installed daemons keep source defaults. They affect MTP scheduling and Qwen speculation, not key custody, attestation, authorization or encryption. I found no change to TB-002, TB-011 or the at-rest cache boundary.

The new benchmark is a ProviderBenchmark target and is a public enum. It loads a model via EngineV2Factory.loadBenchmarkContainer and verifies the weight hash with WeightHasher.computeHash. It builds sessions via makeBenchmarkSession with useProductionKVGrant, requirePersistentKey=false, and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY set to 0 in the passed environment. Because the prefix caches are off, it creates no SSD cache artifacts (T-041) and the TTFT oracle is not extended. Prompts are operator-supplied public strings, not consumer data (A-001). The report emits generated token IDs and timings only to the returned JSON string. The caller may write that to a file, but the caller is outside the supplied evidence. There is no network or coordinator interaction, no registration, and no grant or token handling. Inputs are bounded: batch size 1-64, maxTokens up to 131072, and backend restricted to an allowlist. The only concern is that the modelDirectory config.json read is an operator-local path, which is the local operator's own trust domain. Residual questions for integration: whether the benchmark SPI session paths (@_spi(Benchmarking)) are reachable only from the benchmark CLI and not from the shipped provider, and whether the Package.swift target exposure is unchanged. Neither is supplied here.
